name: Arlington
description: Arlington, often called Oklahoma Rummy, is a complex contract rummy game played over seven distinct hands. It features an aggressive 'wild-stealing' mechanic and a unique 'Offering' phase after every turn, making it much more interactive than standard Draw-and-Discard rummy games.

overview.description: Arlington, often called Oklahoma Rummy, is a complex contract rummy game played over seven distinct hands. It features an aggressive 'wild-stealing' mechanic and a unique 'Offering' phase after every turn, making it much more interactive than standard Draw-and-Discard rummy games.

history.origins: Arlington emerged alongside other contract rummy games like Phase 10 and Liverpool Rummy in the mid-20th century. It became a staple in Oklahoma and the American Midwest specifically for its high-scoring potential.
timeline: 1940s: Early iterations of 'Oklahoma Rummy' appear in social clubs.
1960s: Standardized into the 'Arlington' ruleset with the 'Offering' phase.
Present: Popular in digital rummy collections and regional American card clubs.
history.cultural: Known as a 'long-form' social game, often played during weekend gatherings where the 7-hand progression can be fully appreciated.
history.evolution: The game evolved from basic Rummy by adding 'wild-replacement' rules, where players could liberate wild cards from opponents' melds using natural cards.

setup.deck: 105 cards (2 x 52 + 1 Joker). All 2s and the Joker are wild.
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 13 cards. The remainder forms the stock pile. The top card is flipped to start the discard pile.

rules.objective: Score the most points over seven hands by fulfilling each hand's specific meld contract and eventually 'going rummy' (discarding all cards).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Draw**: Draw the top card of the stock or the discard pile. 2. **Stealing Wilds**: If an opponent has a meld on the table containing a wild card (2 or Joker), and you hold the 'natural' card that wild is representing, you may swap your natural card for that wild and add the wild to your hand. 3. **Melding**: Lay down the specific contract for the current hand. You cannot lay down any other melds until your contract is complete. 4. **Offering**: At the end of your turn, you MUST offer one card from your hand to the table. Starting from your left, each player has a chance to take it and discard a card from their hand to maintain count. 5. **Going Rummy**: To end the hand, you must meld your entire hand and have one card left to discard.
keyRules: Contract Progression: Hand 1 (Two sets of 3); Hand 7 (Three runs of 4). Requirements increase each hand.
Aces & Wilds Offerting: Aces and Wild cards can ONLY be offered to the player on your immediate left. If they don't want it, it goes to the discard pile.
Discard Pile Capture: You can only take the top discard if you use it in a meld immediately.

strategy.basic: Prioritize high-value cards (Jokers) in your melds. If you lose the hand, having a Joker in your hand is a 50-point penalty.
strategy.intermediate: The Offering Phase: Offer cards that are 'dead' to the board (e.g., a card whose duplicates have already been melded or discarded). Never offer a card that helps an opponent complete a run.
strategy.advanced: Wild Hijacking: Keep 'natural' cards that match current wild positions in opponents' melds. Steal the wild only when you are ready to complete your own contract or go rummy.
tips: Wait to lay down your contract until you have almost your whole hand filled. Once you lay down, opponents can steal your wilds!
Hand 7 (Three runs of 4) is the decider; the winning bonus for that hand is usually enough to overcome any early lead.

variations.name: Arlington Queen
variations.description: The Queen of Spades is worth 50 points (same as a Joker) but is NOT wild.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation only changes scoring for the Queen of Spades; no engine config overrides are needed.

variations.name: Short Arlington
variations.description: Played over 6 hands instead of 7 to speed up play.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variation shortens the match length from seven to six hands without changing engine behavior.

scoring.description: Points are earned for cards on the table and subtracted for cards in hand.
scoring.winCondition: Highest total score after seven rounds wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: A premium contract rummy experience involving 105 cards and a marathon seven-hand progression. Master the 'Offering' phase to dump your high-value penalties before someone goes Rummy.
